title: French protesters clash with police in Paris over living costs and schools
seoTitle: Paris march over living costs and schools

tea.why: People are protesting against rising living costs, poor conditions in schools, and declining public services.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand relief from high prices and improvements to public services and schools.
tea.changed: Oct 18: President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm after widespread unrest, while Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported 2,400 arrests and nearly 1,000 injured…

summary: Demonstrations erupted across France, including Paris, as crowds marched to protest rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. Organised by groups including the CGT labour union and student organisations, the marches drew hundreds of thousands of participants nationwide. While many protesters marched peacefully, clashes broke out in cities like Paris, Lyon, and Marseille, involving property damage, fires, and looting. Police responded with tear gas and water cannons. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez attributed the violence to radical groups and criminals seeking confrontation, reporting thousands of arrests and injured officers. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, stating that those responsible would be punished, while acknowledging that peaceful protesters held legitimate grievances.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported thousands of arrests and injured officers, blaming ultra-left groups and criminals for the violence. President Emmanuel Macron condemned the destruction, pledged prosecutions, and appealed for calm.

arrests.text: Police made 2,400 arrests across France, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

injuries.text: nearly 1,000 officers were injured, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.

deaths.text: One protester died on Saturday after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris.

updates.text: Protesters marched across France against rising living costs and school conditions, with clashes occurring in Paris, Lyon, and Marseille.
President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm, and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported 2,400 arrests and nearly 1,000 injured officers.
